name: nested-sections-requirements
body: source spec: feature request "nested sections" (untrusted prose), reconciled against the durable requirements. Contradictions resolved and changes made: (1) requirements.requirement.slide-sections said "Only one level of sections in Markdown" — rewritten so heading depth is nesting depth (# … ######), a section runs to the next same-or-shallower heading, and # notes stays top-level only [autonomous]. (2) requirements.requirement.template-composition said section templates compose "with no depth limit" — rewritten to the same sections: schema slides use, depth bounded at six heading levels, cycles rejected with the chain [autonomous]. (3) section-frontmatter now states the fence is per section at any nesting depth [autonomous]. (4) template-language already claimed sections arrive pre-rendered, but the code (render.renderer.slideData) passes data maps grouped by declared name and never executes a section's layout.html.tmpl; the requirement now states section instances render bottom-up through their own layout, each parent receives child sections as a list of trusted HTML (top-level slide sections too), and section-template-as-field stays data-only [autonomous]. (5) template-context and section-template-context now include the reserved item context; item added to the reserved names (requirements.constraint.reserved-template-names, domain.constraint.template-context-reserved) [autonomous]. (6) template-manifest notes the shared sections: schema and recursive example validation [autonomous]. (7) template-build-checks now enforces depth ≤ 6 and cycle-with-chain [autonomous]. (8) Added requirements.requirement.nested-section-validation (per-parent min/max, full-path errors, recursive example.md, closest-match) and requirements.requirement.item-context (index/number/count/first/last/section/template/parent; nil/absent at slide level) [autonomous]. (9) cli-templates-show now lists a template's child sections and what each accepts, with a nesting tree view as a nice-to-have [autonomous]. Source decision "No backwards compatibility … keep format: 1": recorded — no format migration is authored; domain.value.format and library-manifest stay at 1 [autonomous].
